claim: The actual unchanged MFE retains the authenticated workspace through exactly four controlled hours of accepted mouse renewal, including initial refresh expiry.
limits: Authentication response headers are synthetic. The browser does not validate server signatures or establish live BFF acceptance across four hours.
Headless Edge and controlled clock execution establish neither four elapsed wall-clock hours nor native suspension.
MutationObserver queries current DOM after batched changes. An insertion and removal within one delivery could escape its prompt transition counter.
The trusted mouse count is recorded in each cycle. The runner has no separate explicit assertion on that count.
The same original requirement remains candidate knowledge with human review pending. Passing this controlled criterion does not supply business approval.
reasoning: AC4 explicitly specifies a controlled clock, successful renewals, and accepted activity before each access deadline.
Fifteen-minute access with ten-minute activity permits five minutes of margin at each cycle.
The post-debounce store wait requires more than fourteen minutes of access validity. Previous access has less than five minutes remaining, so a request count alone cannot satisfy it.
Every extension fixture checks the submitted access against the current response credential and requires it to remain valid.
The initial two-hour refresh expiry lies strictly within the exact four-hour assertion interval.
The candidate passes all 128 predicates. Main passes 126 core predicates and fails the extra replacement-refresh retention predicate.
The inherited extra predicate failure does not contradict the separately recorded core AC4 result.
Current source maps bind 137 candidate files and 135 main files, including Home, Axios, response, Timeout and reducer paths.

limitations: JSON syntax, exact runner hashes, counters and retained source-binding reports were inspected.
Automated checks do not check the complete approved dictionary or grammar rules.
